# Arc TV 2.5.0 for Android

- **Up Next.** Continue plays the next episode when one ends, with its code and title on screen.
- **Subtitles when a video has none.** With SubDL on, Arc TV can look for an English subtitle for you as you play,
  and the switch for that lives in Settings; you can also search for one yourself. Two seasons with the same name
  no longer share the wrong cached file.
- **Your SubDL key travels with your backup.** An encrypted backup now carries the SubDL key too, and restoring it never overwrites a key you already have unless you ask.

# Arc TV 2.0.2 (Android and iPhone)

2.0.2 is a small update for the phones.

## What is new

- **Restoring a Mac backup tells you about radio favorites.** The phones cannot play radio yet, so those favorites are skipped. The summary now says how many were skipped instead of dropping them silently.
- **Series match better when the season comes first.** Titles like "2 сезон" or "2nd Season" before or after the name are now understood, and non-English letters are kept when searching.
- **Plainer words.** "Source" instead of "portal" in setup, and one spelling of "favorites" everywhere.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favorites, history, backups, downloads and settings are untouched.
- The Mac app is on 2.2.8.

**What's new in 2.0.1**

- **Choose how many titles the library index keeps:** 1,000, 5,000 (the default), 10,000, 25,000, 50,000 or 100,000. Pick it when you turn the index on, or later under *Title limit* in Settings → Library & details → Title details (TMDB) → Library index.
- **Each choice shows how long a full run takes.** Raising the limit continues where the index stopped. Lowering it keeps the titles already stored; Delete index frees the space.
- **Nothing changes unless you change it.** The default stays at 5,000 and the index stays off until you start it.

The Mac app stays on 2.0.0.

Arc TV 2.0 for Android (early access): Browse by genre with an optional library index, the same new backup file as the Mac (optional passphrase for passwords and your TMDB key), an optional sync folder (Settings → Sync), Up Next, sleep timer, channel schedule, adult-content PIN and accessibility improvements. Updates in place.

Casting live TV to a Samsung TV over DLNA no longer shows "The TV refused the request" while the picture plays: refused position checks are ignored, Play is retried while the TV loads, and the log names any refused action.

Casting to a TV over DLNA no longer closes the app a few seconds in when the TV stops answering or refuses a command: playback shows an error instead, a refused seek is ignored, and the app waits longer on a slow TV.

**Design polish across the app.**

- The home hero now fits phones, tablets, landscape and large text sizes, and the first shelf shows without scrolling.
- Posters show their title on two lines and the year, so similar titles are easy to tell apart.
- One **Cast** button in the player opens a single sheet for Google Cast, DLNA TVs, screen mirroring and your TV's browser. The TV-browser screen no longer has controls drawn over its address.
- Detail has labelled buttons, shows how much is left when you resume, and episodes are cleaner. The player has a Rotate control.
- Search remembers your recent searches and its empty state fits above the keyboard.
- Tab labels stay readable over bright artwork. Update notes, sign-in errors and Settings read in plain language.

**Fix: casting a movie to a browser no longer gives only sound and subtitles.** Safari's own player can't show some HEVC streams (common on IPTV portals) but still reports a picture size, so the page didn't notice.

- The page now checks that video frames are really being drawn, and switches to its own player automatically when they are not.
- Background browser tabs are ignored, so a hidden tab never triggers a false warning.
- Tested with a real portal movie in Safari: the picture now appears after the switch.

The browser or TV needs internet access for the switch.

**Fix: casting to a browser no longer plays only sound.** Some streams carry HEVC video in TS segments, which Safari's own player can't show, so casting to Safari (or a TV browser) gave sound with no picture.

- The page now switches to its own player automatically and carries on from the same spot.
- If a browser still can't show the picture, the page and your phone say so, with the video's format.

The browser or TV needs internet access for the switch.

**One Cast button.** The player used to have three buttons for putting the video on a TV. It now has one, **Cast to TV**.

- It opens a single sheet that lists the Google Cast and DLNA TVs on your Wi-Fi together. Tap one to connect.
- Below the list: **Screen mirroring…** opens your phone's own cast screen for Miracast TVs, and **TV not listed?** shows an address to open in your TV's browser.
- While you are casting, the sheet says who you are casting to and has a Stop button.

Phone and TV need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

**Play on TV, without extra hardware.** For TVs that Google Cast and Miracast don't reach, the player has a new Play on TV button.

- It lists the DLNA TVs on your Wi-Fi. Tap one and the video plays there while your phone keeps the controls.
- TV not listed? The same sheet shows a short address to open in your TV's own browser, and the video plays there. Pausing or stopping hands the position back to your phone.
- If a TV refuses a stream, the player says so and points you to the browser option.

Phone and TV need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

**Fixes and polish:** watch progress is now kept per season (episode 1 of season 2 no longer overwrites episode 1 of season 1). Settings is simpler: five clear sections and a "Show advanced settings" switch. The player is easier to use on a phone: a roomier title, one More menu, a clean failed-playback screen, a seek bar that screen readers can use. Search says so when the network failed instead of "No results", episodes get a Try Again button, poster grids fill the screen evenly, text is easier to read, and error messages are in plain words.

**Fix:** shows whose portal lists a season in pages now show every episode. Some portals send 14 at a time, newest first, so the oldest episodes (like Season 1 Episode 1) were missing; the same applies to shows with many seasons.

**Arc TV for Android** 0.1.8 (early access). Phones and tablets, Android 8.0 or newer.

**What's new:** the app can now update itself. Open **Settings → Updates** to check, download and install new versions, and
Arc TV looks for updates when it opens (you can turn that off). Also in this build: the floating glass tab bar, portal
export, Miracast, per-season downloads, live channels in Search, and a Series tab with its own categories.
